colt.d.ramsey: Zeno Ramsey unpacked a lock of hair in a matchbox at S-F17. A neighbour shifted a bag to make room without asking what it was. Day 3. Verdel Ridge fell to the Concord. Zeno Ramsey watched their flag go up on the heights and dug his trench a little deeper.
Otto Carlingiti and Zeno Ramsey split the last tin of beef, counting the bites out loud to keep it fair.
Zeno Ramsey heard wire rattling beyond the parapet. At the change of watch, he said exactly where and asked for it to be taken seriously.

A bullet clipped Zeno Ramsey's helmet at S-F17 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. Shot by Bram Archiegregor of the Concord (@archiegregorysmith). On Day 6, Hill 304 passed to the Hegemony. Zeno Ramsey wrote the name in his diary with unusual care.
The medics cleaned Zeno Ramsey's wound one last time and pronounced him fit. He is back to full duty at S-F17.
Zeno Ramsey found a photograph in the mud of no man's land: a wedding party, and a name on the back that is not from his side of the wire.
Zeno Ramsey saved half a biscuit for later. Later came six minutes afterwards.
Zeno Ramsey reached up to fix a sandbag at S-F17 and a bullet took the skin off two knuckles. The sandbag got fixed anyway. Shot by Felix "Spark" Toastybweady of the Concord (@toastybweady).
erwin_schwols: Pavel Schwols came from Dunmarrow, where there is a river, a church and no mud at all. He talks about all three as if they were people.
finland2438: Benedikt Finland came up on Day 5 carrying news from Greyhallow. A man interrupted to ask whether the railway clock had been repaired.

Benedikt Finland sorted the dressings by lamplight. When the next stretcher arrived, he could find everything without looking. The Hegemony secured Hill 304. Benedikt Finland helped pass the news along the line, checking each time that he had heard correctly.
An unexploded shell lay beside the approach trench. Benedikt Finland helped steer the carrying party around it and was glad to leave the problem to somebody else.
Someone had used a newspaper to wrap the onions. Benedikt Finland read a theatre review while peeling supper.
Benedikt Finland was hit in the foot through his boot at R-F1. The boot had to be cut off. He asked them to save the other one. Shot by Gustav "Spark" Echoss of the Concord (@echoss_3).
The bearers moved Benedikt Finland's stretcher against the wall at midday and back again at dusk. That was the whole schedule.
gndr_bliss: Pavel Bliss walked into R-S13 on Day 7 and asked where the war was. A shell answered before anyone else could. Pavel Bliss left the work of a stretcher bearer to become a sapper. Someone from the old section came over to see how it was going.

A stretcher party needed the passage. Pavel Bliss backed into a recess with an ammunition box and stayed there until the last bearer passed. A letter from home found Pavel Bliss before the night shift. Pavel Bliss folded it small and kept it close.

Pavel Bliss of the Hegemony and Severin Guy of the Concord share the same habit: a whistle at midnight. Both lines at the Drowned Farm now wait for it before they sleep. A letter from home found Pavel Bliss before the night shift. Pavel Bliss folded it small and kept it close.
luckycat2025: On Day 9 Florian Luckycat took a post at R-C7 that had been empty for two nights. He did not ask why. He hates silence more than shelling, and the men liked him for it.
ner_small: The sergeant gave Walter Small a dead man's blanket and a living man's job. That is how replacements start, on Day 3 or any other.
Walter Small raised his head for a heartbeat too long at S-F18. The bullet only grazed him. He will not do it again. Shot by Marek "Brick" Buddy of the Concord (@big_fat_buddy).
A medic checked Walter Small's dressing at S-F18 and said he would be back on his feet soon. He was already trying to stand.

Stitches out, sleeve rolled down. Walter Small is whole again, or near enough for the line. Hill 304 fell to the Hegemony at dusk. Walter Small helped drag the guns up the slope and slept that night on ground nobody else had held for years.
The new recruit kept closing both eyes to aim. Walter Small spent the afternoon helping until one eye stayed open.
A bullet clipped Walter Small's helmet at S-F18 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. Shot by Marek "Brick" Buddy of the Concord (@big_fat_buddy).
Walter Small no longer winces when he lifts his rifle. The medic signed him off with a grunt.

A bullet hit the sandbag next to Walter Small's ear at S-F18 and sprayed his face with grit and blood. A scratch, the medic said, and a lucky one. Shot by Felix "Spark" Toastybweady of the Concord (@toastybweady).
power_armor_bob: At the depot, Norbert Bob had practised answering to his name. At S-R13, the first person to call it only wanted help with a crate.
tavin_anderson: Teodor Anderson signed the papers with a steady hand. The trench at R-C16 took him in like it takes everyone: without a word.
